## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and validation harness

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format — package metadata, pinned image references, and a validation manifest — so that tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases, and delivers the validation harness that checks a packaged tutorial against a target platform release. This is the foundation the tutorial gallery and every curated tutorial are built against.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial package metadata (tutorial identity, version, core journey description, launch target type)
- Define the pinned image reference policy for tutorial notebooks so content runs against known-good images
- Define the validation manifest describing how a packaged tutorial is tested against a release
- Provide a validation harness that validates a packaged tutorial against a target release and reports a pass/fail result
- The format must support both workbench (notebook) tutorials and pipeline tutorials

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written format specification exists covering package metadata, pinned image references, and the validation manifest
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be run through the validation harness against a target release, producing a deterministic pass/fail result
- The format supports both launch target types: workbench (notebook) tutorials and pipeline tutorials
- A tutorial's version and validation status can change without requiring a Dashboard release (packaging is independent of Dashboard release cadence)
- The portion of the format specification covering the pipeline launch target type is reviewed and signed off by the RHOAI Pipelines team (the team whose tutorial content and tooling build against the format but do not co-own it), with the sign-off recorded on the specification

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, primary): tutorial packaging format defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases
- Enables HLR-1 and HLR-2: the gallery and all curated tutorials are built against this format

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch

## Description

Adds a curated tutorial gallery to the Dashboard from which a user can launch a tutorial into their own project with one click: opening a workbench preloaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines application. The gallery renders and launches tutorials packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images).

## Scope

- Tutorial gallery surface in the Dashboard listing packaged tutorials, driven by tutorial package metadata
- One-click launch of a notebook tutorial: spawns a workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook available
- One-click launch of a pipeline tutorial: imports the pipeline into the user's project
- Consumption of tutorial packages per the packaging format (metadata, pinned image references)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can browse the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and see tutorial entries rendered with their metadata from at least one tutorial packaged per the tutorial packaging format (the gallery is metadata-driven; the full curated set is not a prerequisite of this epic)
- Launching a notebook tutorial creates a workbench in the user's project with the tutorial notebook available and running (validates the Notebooks component keeps working with no code changes on it — passive component)
- Launching a pipeline tutorial imports the pipeline into the user's project's Data Science Pipelines application (validates the Data Science Pipelines component keeps working with no code changes on it — passive component)
- Gallery rendering and both launch paths are verified end-to-end against at least one tutorial packaged per the tutorial packaging format

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0, primary): Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch into the user's project

# Author five notebook-based curated tutorials

## Scope

- Author the first-workbench tutorial (notebook content)
- Author the data-prep tutorial (notebook content)
- Author the first-training-run tutorial (notebook content)
- Author the first-deployment tutorial (notebook content; exercises existing model-serving capabilities without changing them)
- Author the first-RAG-app tutorial (notebook content; exercises existing serving and storage capabilities without changing them)
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format, with pinned images and a validation manifest
- Run each tutorial through the validation harness against the current release

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist, one per journey listed in scope, each packaged per the tutorial packaging format
- Each tutorial passes validation against the current release via the validation harness
- The first-workbench tutorial is verified end-to-end in a workbench in a user project (validates the Notebooks component keeps working — passive component)
- Each tutorial is versioned so it can be re-validated and updated independently of Dashboard releases

## HLR Traceability

# Document gallery usage and tutorial contribution process

## Description

Writes the user and contributor documentation for the tutorial gallery: how to use the gallery (browse the curated set, launch a tutorial into your project) and the contribution process for new tutorials (packaging per the format, validation, and curation review). This is a docs-authoring epic running through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

- Doc topic: using the tutorial gallery — browsing curated tutorials and launching them into a project (workbench with notebook, or pipeline import)
- Doc topic: the contribution process for new tutorials — packaging requirements per the tutorial packaging format, validation against a release, and the curation/review path
- Outline and draft the topics, then finalize them against the shipped gallery and tutorial set

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the tutorial gallery end to end (browse, launch notebook tutorial, launch pipeline tutorial)
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials, including packaging and validation requirements
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and the shipped tutorial set (reviewed by the implementing teams)
- Documentation does not describe submission tooling as available — the contribution process is documented but intake tooling is out of scope for this release

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials
